name: Vaultwarden
tagline: A lightweight community server for the Bitwarden apps
description: An independent, compatible implementation of the Bitwarden server, written in Rust. You keep using the official Bitwarden apps and browser extensions, but point them at a small server of your own.
backing: A community project led by volunteer maintainers; not affiliated with Bitwarden, Inc.

maturity.rationale: Hugely popular among self-hosters for years and actively maintained. It is an unofficial reimplementation, though: it has had far less independent security review than Bitwarden's own server, and support for new client features sometimes lags.

selfHosting.summary: One small container and a reverse proxy with HTTPS. The software is the easy part. You become the sole guardian of every password you own, so off-site backups and prompt updates are not optional.

strengths: Needs very little memory or processor
Works with the official Bitwarden apps and browser extensions
Includes features that are paid on Bitwarden's own server, such as organisations and one-time codes
A single container with SQLite by default, so backups are simple
weaknesses: Unofficial: compatibility depends on keeping up with Bitwarden's clients, and occasionally breaks until patched
Far less independent security review than Bitwarden's server
An exposed, unpatched instance is a high-value target, and that risk is yours

featureNotes.audited: The clients are Bitwarden's audited ones; the server has had limited review
